game.name: Hades
game.short_description: Defy the god of the dead as you hack and slash out of the Underworld in this rogue-like dungeon crawler from the creators of Bastion, Transistor, and Pyre.

other_scores.score: about $304M gross / about $89.7M net; SteamSpy owners 5M-10M

placements.verbal_evidence: this game definitely deserves to be S tier it's an absolute Masterpiece

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Hades is Supergiant's 2018 early-access-era roguelite that surprised everyone and, in his view, deserves all its hype. He has speedrun it and once placed in the top 100 of a run category. He calls it a masterpiece and probably the best roguelike on the board so far, and he places it in S tier without hesitation.
praise: Huge run-start customization: many boons/passes, weapons with unique abilities, keepsakes/charms, companions
Replayability: never gets old, he can always come back to it
Art style and visual effects are amazing
Every line of text is voice acted, with a great volume of dialogue
Speedrunning scene gives it lasting depth
criticism: No real criticisms; he says he wishes he could put games in S tier that are not truly S, implying Hades clearly earns it
unique_points: Fully voiced narrative integrated into a roguelite at massive scale
Per-run difficulty customization and starting-loadout variety keep runs fresh
commentary.quote: it's an absolute Masterpiece this is uh honestly probably the best roguelike so far
design_criteria: Customization/build variety: weapons, boons, keepsakes, companions give differing starts
Audio: full voice acting on every line

community.one_liner: Supergiant Games' isometric action roguelite in which Zagreus, son of Hades, fights out of the Greek Underworld, with story and dialogue woven into the run-and-die loop.
community.consensus_summary: Hades is treated as a landmark of the genre by both critics and players: Metacritic 93 from 58 critic reviews with no mixed or negative ones, Steam 'Overwhelmingly Positive' at about 98% of roughly 309k reviews, and Wikipedia reports 99% of critics recommending it on OpenCritic. It swept Game of the Year at BAFTA, DICE, GDC and other ceremonies and became the first video game to win a Hugo. It spent almost two years in early access (from Dec 2018) and then launched in full in Sept 2020 to very strong sales. The main dissent comes from players who bounce off the roguelite structure itself (repetition, fixed biomes and bosses, RNG, meta-grind), not from the craft. Metacritic user score is lower than critics at 8.5, with Metacritic's summary citing RNG frustration and repetitive restarts.
best_things: Story is delivered through the run loop: each death brings new hub dialogue, so failure advances the narrative and feels rewarding rather than punishing
Fast, fluid, responsive combat with six distinct weapons and several aspects each, praised as weighty and satisfying
Boon system from the Olympian gods gives build variety and synergies (duo boons) while staying compact enough to understand
Writing, voice acting and characterisation are repeatedly singled out, including Zagreus's politeness and the gods' interplay and relationships
Art direction by Jen Zee and the soundtrack are near-universal praise
Accessible for roguelike newcomers: God Mode quietly boosts you after each death, and the hub and mirror upgrades soften early losses
Heat / Pact of Punishment gives scalable endgame difficulty and long replay value
Many reviewers who dislike the genre say this was the one that hooked them
worst_things: Only four biomes and a fixed set of bosses, so runs feel samey after a few dozen hours
Final boss fight against Hades is a big difficulty spike, frustrating to some players on the True Ending route
RNG in boon and reward offers can make runs feel unfair or throttle progress
Reviewers who want Binding of Isaac style emergent builds find boons mostly stat bonuses and percentages with few memorable or wild builds
Reaching full narrative closure (epilogue) takes very many clears; only a small share of players get there
Some players find the combat button-mashy, with heavy area damage, projectile spam and particle clutter (the lava biome and its bombers are a named pain point)
improvements: More biomes, bosses and enemy variety to reduce repetition (partly answered by Hades II)
Stronger, more game-changing boons or build-defining items for wilder synergies
A less grindy route to the epilogue and to late resources such as Titan Blood
Heat system that adds new mechanics rather than mostly limiting options or raising numbers
Clearer tracking of upgrade shop contents and rewards; several negative reviewers complain that remembering every god's offerings is hard
Finer-grained difficulty and assist options than God Mode's fixed ramp; one reviewer wanted an initial armour setting like Hades II
unique_things: Narrative-first roguelite: dialogue, relationships and plot progress are the meta-progression alongside stat unlocks
Greek mythology cast reinterpreted with personality-driven, sympathetic gods
Protagonist who is meant to die: death returns you to a living hub home with characters who react to how you died
God Mode accessibility that scales up with each failure, so the story is reachable for anyone
Pact of Punishment and heat let you tailor difficulty with many modifiers and unlock cosmetic rewards
Release-quality polish from a two-year early access that shipped with full voice acting and music
tedious_or_disliked: Running the same four regions and bosses many times to reach the story's ending
Grinding for meta resources such as Titan Blood and diamonds late in the game, described as a chore
Dodging heavy AoE and projectile spam in the later rooms, called monotonous by some
Heat-stacking runs where the added difficulty feels like restricted options rather than fresh play
Story interruptions and hub trips feel like hurdles to players who just want to start the next run; some later realise they are the point
Some users compare the loop to habit-forming or gambling-style design
divisive_points: Roguelite meta-progression: many find it a gentle learning curve, purists feel it hides whether they are actually improving
Story gating and repetition: praised as integrated and rewarding by most, but a slog by others (e.g. 70+ hours with little left to see)
Boon depth: fans praise clear synergies, critics say few builds are memorable compared with Isaac or Slay the Spire
Difficulty: hard at first, then manageable for most players, but the final boss and high heat frustrate some
community.reception_notes: Early access began 6 Dec 2018 after a Game Awards reveal; Wikipedia cites about 700k copies during nearly two years of early access and another 300k in three days after the 17 Sept 2020 full release (over 1M total then; later third-party estimates are far higher). Launch on PC (Windows, macOS) and Switch; PS4/PS5 and Xbox arrived 13 Aug 2021; a Netflix Games mobile version ran from March 2024 until it was removed in July 2025. Cross-save between Windows and Switch came via a Dec 2020 patch. Won GOTY at BAFTA, DICE, GDC, New York Game Awards and SXSW, plus a Hugo. Current Steam reviews are still highly positive, with the sequel Hades II drawing players back to the original. Note: OpenCritic's exact average was not retrievable in this session (WebSearch budget exhausted and the game page could not be located), so it is left null.
